title: Speranza’s plaintive muse
html_source: This refers to the pen name of Lady Jane Wilde, who not only gave birth to her famous literary son Oscar, but was a poet of some fame herself. Her activism for Irish independence led to her being considered “Speranza of the Nation.” Her poem To Ireland, contained the kind of extreme passionate nationalism that Joyce seems to be lampooning in this parody. Robert Emmet, whose public funeral the parody supposedly describes, was executed in 1803, eighteen years prior to Lady Jane’s birth. There was, in fact, no public funeral for Emmet. Joyce was wary of such excessive emotionalism would devolve into kitsch.
